content: A change of the instruments has the effect of a melody, even on one pitch. In later use: one line goes from instrument to instrument
parameters: Webern: frequently one note for each instrument
example: Schoenberg, Five Pieces op. 16 no. 3 (1909). Webern, Five Pieces op. 10 (1913)

content: The chord C, G-sharp, B, E, A stays. The instruments that play it change: "a kaleidoscopically rotating array of instrumental colors"
parameters: Schoenberg to the conductor: "There are no motives in this piece which have to be brought to the fore"

content: "The simultaneous variation of a single melodic line": some players have the plain line, others have it with ornaments or in a different rhythm
parameters: Usual in gamelan, gagaku, and Arab classical music

content: Many lines in canon at different speeds. The ear cannot follow one line: the result is a cluster that moves
parameters: Cope: it differs from a cluster "in its use of moving rather than static lines"

content: All notes are written. The players do not play exactly together: each player goes at his own speed until the conductor gives a sign
parameters: The composer controls the harmony and the form. Lutosławski: "I do not presuppose any improvised parts"
example: Lutosławski, Jeux vénitiens (1960-61). Hovhaness (1958): "Repeat and repeat ad lib, but not together"

content: Two strands of music overlap as the links of a chain: one strand starts before the other stops
parameters: The sections do not start and stop together

content: Texture, tone colour, and loudness are more important than the single pitches
parameters: Clusters, glissandi, extreme registers, flutter-tongue, mutes

content: A new tempo comes from a note value of the old tempo: the pivot note value is the same in the two tempos
parameters: New tempo = old tempo x (number of pivot notes in the new bar / number in the old bar). Example: 84 x 3/2 = 126

content: The number of notes for each beat grows and then becomes smaller again
example: Bartók, Music for Strings, Percussion and Celesta III (xylophone)

content: Each instrument plays one partial of a sound. The pitches come from the harmonic series and can be microtones
"Sunrise is represented by an orchestral tutti beginning with pointillistic night sounds". A very large crescendo breaks off. Then "a soft, warm string chord" is the risen sun
parameters: Points of sound; one crescendo; a sudden stop; one soft chord

content: The orchestra part is as difficult as the solo part: the work "approaches being a concerto for orchestra"
parameters: Each section and many single players get a display passage
example: Corigliano, Clarinet Concerto. Bartók, Concerto for Orchestra

device: Section borders that are not sharp
content: The parts of the form go into each other. The listener does not hear the exact moment of the change
